record.context_brief: Jump behavior of normalized Cauchy transforms
record.original_question: For f in L^2(mu_gamma), can one control the jump across the unit circle of the normalized Cauchy transform of f mu_gamma, and can that control be used to generalize the connection with pseudocontinuation?

evidence.quote: Open problems: Is it possible to control the jump of the normalized Cauchy transform of fµγ, f ∈ L2(µγ)?
This may be useful for generalizing the connection to pseudocontinuation, see Section 7 below.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma$ be an inner function on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ (i.e., a bounded holomorphic function on $\mathbb{D}$ whose nontangential boundary values have modulus $1$ almost everywhere on $\mathbb{T}=\partial\mathbb{D}$), and let $\mu_\gamma$ denote the Clark measure on $\mathbb{T}$ associated with $\gamma$, defined as the unique positive Borel measure on $\mathbb{T}$ satisfying
$$\mathrm{Re}\,\frac{1+\overline{\gamma(0)}\,\gamma(z)}{1-\overline{\gamma(0)}\,\gamma(z)}=\int_{\mathbb{T}}\frac{1-|z|^2}{|\zeta-z|^2}\,d\mu_\gamma(\zeta),\qquad z\in\mathbb{D}.$$
For $f\in L^2(\mu_\gamma)$, the normalized Cauchy transform of $f\mu_\gamma$ is the function
$$V_\gamma f(z)=\frac{1}{1-\gamma(z)}\int_{\mathbb{T}}\frac{1-\overline{\gamma(0)}}{1-\bar\zeta z}\,f(\zeta)\,d\mu_\gamma(\zeta),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{T},$$
which defines a holomorphic function both inside $\mathbb{D}$ and on the exterior $\mathbb{D}_e=\{|z|>1\}\cup\{\infty\}$ (vanishing at $\infty$).

Question: For every $f\in L^2(\mu_\gamma)$, can one quantitatively control the jump
$$J_f(\zeta)=\lim_{r\to 1^-}\bigl(V_\gamma f(r\zeta)-V_\gamma f(\zeta/r)\bigr)$$
of $V_\gamma f$ across the unit circle in terms of $f$ and $\mu_\gamma$? Furthermore, can such a jump estimate be used to extend the known correspondence between $V_\gamma f$ and pseudocontinuation (i.e., the property that the inner and outer boundary values of $V_\gamma f$ coincide as nontangential limits almost everywhere on $\mathbb{T}$) to this $L^2(\mu_\gamma)$ setting?
artifact.category_tag: Normalized Cauchy transforms and Clark measures
artifact.status_search_result: A search did not surface a definitive published resolution of the question of controlling the jump across $\mathbb{T}$ of the normalized Cauchy transform $V_\gamma f$ for general $f\in L^2(\mu_\gamma)$, nor a corresponding $L^2$ extension of the pseudocontinuation correspondence. Standard references (Cima–Matheson–Ross, "The Cauchy Transform"; Poltoratski's work on boundary behavior of pseudocontinuable functions; Aleksandrov's papers) treat related boundary-value and pseudocontinuation results, but the specific jump-control problem in $L^2(\mu_\gamma)$ does not appear to be settled in the literature located.

status_evidence.title: The Cauchy Transform (Cima, Matheson, Ross)
status_evidence.snippet: Chapter 10 is dedicated to the normalized Cauchy transform; for sigma_alpha-almost every zeta the non-tangential limit equals f(zeta).
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference establishing boundary behavior of the normalized Cauchy transform but not addressing the jump-control problem in L^2(mu_gamma).

status_evidence.title: Maximal properties of the normalized Cauchy transform (Poltoratski)
status_evidence.snippet: Maximal and boundary-behavior results for the normalized Cauchy transform.
status_evidence.claim: Related boundary-behavior results exist but do not provide the requested jump control.
